searchText: <@363800010518822915> <@755590043632140352> gmgm some slots report this error, missing block proposals: vc: ``` [2026-05-21 10:07:51.18] ERROR client: Failed to request block from beacon node error=rpc error: code = Internal desc = could not build block in parallel: rpc error: code = Internal desc = Could not get local payload: could not get cached payload from execution client: got an unexpected error in JSON-RPC response: invalid character 'm' after array element pubkey=0x8d1543bcda5c slot=88 ``` bn ``` [2026-05-21 10:07:51.17] ERROR rpc/validator: Finished building block error=rpc error: code = Internal desc = Could not get local payload: could not get cached payload from execution client: got an unexpected error in JSON-RPC response: invalid character 'm' after array element sinceSlotStartTime=174.566883ms slot=88 validator=395 ``` seems like a one off thing still pretty weird, any idea what might cause it? Oh really weird, may be an EL thing looking into it hmm might be a snooper bug Snooper logs: ```sh ERRO[2026-05-21T10:07:51Z] call failed: proxy response stream error: read tcp 172.16.0.20:55242->172.16.0.11:8551: use of closed network connection 2026/05/21 10:07:51 http: superfluous response.WriteHeader call from github.com/urfave/negroni.(*responseWriter).WriteHeader (response_writer.go:53) INFO[2026-05-21T10:07:51Z] REQUEST #393: POST / length=89 method=engine_getPayloadV6 type=json { "id": 392, "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "engine_getPayloadV6", "params": [ "0x6c938e742fa27d90" ] } WARN[2026-05-21T10:07:51Z] failed unmarshaling data: unexpected end of JSON input INFO[2026-05-21T10:07:51Z] RESPONSE #393: POST / duration_ms=6 length=-1 status=200 type=unknown 0x7b226a736f6e727063223a22322e3022...35356538356630363163393137303465 <32768 bytes> ``` cc <@808969530608451584> ever seen this before ? looks like the response is cut off. check the hex with a ascii converter: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0"`...`55e85f061c91704e` there is no closing bracket at the end, looks like cut off within a value will look shortly i think snooper's upstream conn to the EL got force-closed mid-response (the "use of closed network connection" line). it had already started streaming 200 + bytes back to prysm, then tried to overwrite the status when the upstream died that's the "superfluous WriteHeader"
